files.purpose: This is the static HTML shell for the Droppy marketing website's 'Changelog' page (getdroppycode.app/changelog.html): a hand-duplicated copy of index.html's <head> boilerplate, fixed nav pill and footer (the file's own top comment says so explicitly, line 5: 'kept identical with index.html by hand: edit them everywhere or nowhere'), wrapping one empty content region (#changelog-root) that assets/js/changelog.js fills at page-load time by fetching website/changelog.json. It carries no release-note text itself — all per-version content is data, loaded at runtime from a sibling JSON file generated by scripts/build_changelog.py from CHANGELOG.md — so the HTML's only job is chrome (nav/hero/loading-state/footer) around that runtime-filled list.
key_symbols: #apple-mark inline SVG <symbol> (shared Apple mark used by every 'for macOS' pill)
changelog-hero / changelog-hero__inner / section-heading / section-subtitle (reveal-on-load elements with --reveal-delay inline styles)
footer__brand / footer__grid / footer__col x4 (Menu, Droppy, Open source, Connect) / footer__wordmark
calls_into: assets/js/changelog.js?v=3 (fetches and renders website/changelog.json into #changelog-root; not itself read in this bundle)
side_effects: Inline <script> in <head> (line 52) reads/writes sessionStorage key 'droppyCodeNavIntro' to skip the nav-intro reveal animation on repeat views in the same tab, wrapped in try/catch so a blocked/unavailable sessionStorage is silently ignored.
platform_assumptions: The footer byline copy (line 124) advertises 'one Liquid Glass window on Apple silicon' and the nav/footer link only to a macOS download (/download/latest, 'Download for macOS' with an Apple-mark SVG) — this is macOS/Apple-silicon marketing language with no Windows equivalent, but it describes the public website for the original Droppy Code product, not the Windows app's own UI.
persisted_fields: sessionStorage['droppyCodeNavIntro'] (browser tab-local, marketing site only, not app data)
ui_elements: Fixed top nav pill: logo+wordmark link to index.html, four section links (Hydra/Features/Changelog[current]/FAQ), a menu toggle button, and a 'Download' CTA button
Hero block: kicker with small icon + 'Release notes' label, H1 'Changelog', subtitle sentence
Content region: initially a centered loading state (spinner + 'Loading release notes...' text) inside an aria-live region, replaced at runtime by assets/js/changelog.js with the actual release list

Footer: brand block (logo, tagline, description, 'Download for macOS' CTA, copyright with live year, 'Built with ... Jordy Spruit' byline, 'made by Droppy' line) plus four link columns (Menu, Droppy, Open source, Connect) and a large background wordmark
feature_notes: The entire B2->B3 diff (`git -C E:\Droppy\reference\droppy-code-v1.7.0 diff 1fbf81e61e28a079508a074c01ee1830a9cc23dc HEAD -- website/changelog.html`) is a 6-line/3-line-pair cache-bust: the query suffix on the shared OG image URL (https://getdroppycode.app/assets/og/og-home.png) changed from '?v=2' to '?v=3' in three places — <meta property="og:image">, <meta property="og:image:secure_url">, and <meta name="twitter:image"> (og:image:alt/twitter:image:alt text is unchanged). This is a website-asset version bump for social-preview cache-busting, presumably because og-home.png itself was refreshed for the 1.7.0 marketing cycle; the asset image itself is out of this bundle's file list, so its visual content was not inspected here.
No other line changed: line count is unchanged at 178, and the nav, hero copy, loading-state markup, footer copy and every href are byte-identical to B2.

This file is classified 'first_party_website' / 'not_in_app_target' in porting/source_inventory.json (build_inclusion) — it is required reading under CLAUDE.md's mandatory-reading list (website/) but is never compiled into or shipped with the Windows app; it is the public marketing site, hosted separately (netlify.toml) from the DroppyCode.app / Marrow Code binary.

C-04 in porting/instruction_conflicts.md establishes that CHANGELOG.md's structure (via scripts/build_changelog.py) feeds the app's own About/update cards as a genuine parity requirement, but that is a separate code path (CHANGELOG.md -> build_changelog.py -> the app's About/update UI) from this marketing-site HTML page, which instead is consumed by website/assets/js/changelog.js fetching website/changelog.json for the public website only.
unresolved_questions: og-home.png (the image whose cache-busting query param changed) is not part of this bundle; whether its pixel content changed between B2 and B3 was not checked here and would need its own binary-asset bundle to confirm — it has no bearing on the Windows port either way since this whole file is out of the app build target.
